title: Save Hilltop School — Final Eco Challenge
scenario: You are visiting Hilltop School, a DIFFERENT fictional school from Sunny School. The school has a garden, canteen, library and recycling corner. Its stated collection rules: clean paper and empty cans can be recycled; fruit scraps can go to an onsite compost collection; mixed snack wrappers go to general waste. Facilities may differ at real schools.

questions.prompt: A tap is dripping after everyone leaves. What is the issue?
The canteen throws away unopened extra snacks each day. What might this indicate?
Why can using a refillable drink bottle matter?
options: It means water cannot be wasted

questions.prompt: A box of clean writing paper is being thrown away. What should the school consider?
options: Whether pages can be used again or recycled

questions.prompt: The school wants fewer disposable drink containers. Which trial is sensible?
A classroom folder has a loose fastener. What could happen before buying a replacement?
options: Ask an adult whether it can be repaired

questions.prompt: Lunch portions are often left uneaten. Which first step gives useful evidence?
options: Ask students about portion needs and observe leftovers

questions.prompt: Where should clean paper go under Hilltop School's rules when it cannot be reused?
A tap seems broken. What is the safe action for a Grade 4 student?
options: Leave it running and do nothing

questions.prompt: Which waste category is largest in Hilltop School's fictional audit?
In the sample, how many percentage points larger is food (40%) than paper (20%)?
If the sample contains 100 items, how many are classified as packaging at 30%?
On the fictional map, which direction from the centre is the garden?
Which first action follows from food being the largest category in this sample?
options: Investigate lunch leftovers and portion sizes
Assume every school has the same waste pattern

sections.title: Explain your plan
sections.prompt: Suggest one realistic change Hilltop School could trial to reduce unnecessary waste or resource use. Use at least one finding from the fictional audit or the map. Explain who would help and why your plan might work.

rubric.criterion: Clear justification including who or how

instructions: A new practice example, not a validated VCAA assessment. Auto-grade only closed items; report the written 6 marks as pending teacher review.
